Below the text, a centred italic heading, then a paragraph in smaller type that forms a commentary below the main text. A catchword at the lower right. A signature at the lower left.

main_text.p: "EO PRONEPOS, &c. Sed etsi uiuo filio, iam mortuo {*}pronepo-te. nepote, cuius uxor prægnas essèt, testamentum faceret, p o test dicere, SI ME VIVO FILIVS DECEDAT, TVNC QVI PRONEPOS. Num si & filius & nepos uiuat, concipere utriusque mortuis, uiuo se, tunc qui pronepos nasceretur? quod similiter admittendum est. ita safe nè, si prius nepos, deinde filius decederet, ne successione testamentum rumperetur."
Idem credendum est.) Tres proponit casus, quibus institui pronepos possit, ad quos hanc pertinere formulam demonstrat: cum aut filio mortuo nepos,

page.notes: Printed line-initial quotation marks (») were not all reliably legible; the passage is given as one paragraph. The word "safe" is a printed line-end form of "sa-nè", with the hyphen before "nè" lost in the scan; check against the original. "essèt" and "testamentum" have a printed accent or tilde; read as the scan shows. The "p o test" spacing is as printed. The running head is too faint to read. The small circled symbol in the left margin beside the commentary is a printer's mark and was not transcribed. The catchword "aut" is printed at the lower right and was not repeated in the text. The signature "Cc 4" is partly obscured.
